title.value: Consensus meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
title.quote: # Consensus meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias

design.value: Consensus fixed-effects meta-analysis of European-ancestry genome-wide association studies of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, across the EADB, IGAP and PGC-ALZ consortia plus UK Biobank and FinnGen, with no-proxy and no-biobank sensitivity meta-analyses
design.quote: To better characterize the genetic architecture underlying Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related dementias (ADRD), we performed a meta-analysis of European-ancestry genome-wide association studies in 128,681 cases or proxy cases of ADRD and 849,833 (proxy) controls.

n.quote: we performed a meta-analysis of European-ancestry genome-wide association studies in 128,681 cases or proxy cases of ADRD and 849,833 (proxy) controls

n_description.value: Cases or proxy cases of ADRD (128,681), counted separately from the 849,833 (proxy) controls; the document breaks this down as 72,721 AD cases, 55,960 proxy ADRD cases, 614,267 controls and 235,566 proxy controls from 52 studies, corresponding to a rough effective sample size of 230,631
n_description.quote: The meta-analysis included 72,721 AD cases, 55,960 proxy ADRD cases, 614,267 controls and 235,566 proxy controls from 52 studies, corresponding to a rough effective sample size of 230,631

population.value: European-ancestry participants from 52 studies: clinically diagnosed AD cases, biobank cases identified by International Classification of Diseases codes, and proxy ADRD cases (individuals reporting at least one biological relative, parent or sibling, affected with dementia), plus controls and proxy controls
population.quote: We analyzed genotyping data from European-ancestry samples across 52 studies—46 case–control or cohort studies, 2 family studies (NIA-LOAD and Framingham Heart Study (FHS)) and 4 large biobanks (UKBB, FinnGen, deCODE and HUNT).

comparator.value: Controls and proxy controls; in the UK Biobank, proxy status was based on reporting a biological relative affected with dementia
comparator.quote: In the UKBB, proxy ADRD cases included participants who reported at least one biological relative (parent or siblings) affected with dementia, either at baseline or follow-up

cohorts: Alzheimer’s Disease Centers/National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (ADC/NACC)

outcomes.name: Number of genome-wide significant (tier 1) loci associated with ADRD risk in the main meta-analysis
outcomes.effect_estimate: 91 tier 1 loci, of which 16 new in European-ancestry samples and 56 associated with clinically diagnosed AD
outcomes.quote: In summary, this consensus meta-analysis identified 91 genetic loci associated with ADRD risk, including 16 new loci in European-ancestry samples, and 56 of the loci were associated with the risk of clinically diagnosed AD.

outcomes.name: Loci new in European-ancestry samples at the time of analysis
outcomes.effect_estimate: 16 new tier 1 loci (EIF4G3, PTPRC, MGAT5, PPP2R3A, ADGRL3, FAM193B, TMEM184A, DOCK4, IPMK, UBFD1, VMAC, VAV1, LRRC25, CEP89, LILRB1/LILRB4 and SRC)
outcomes.quote: We identified 91 genetic loci associated with ADRD risk, of which 16 are new and 56 are specifically detected in clinically diagnosed AD cases.

outcomes.name: Tier 2 loci requiring further external validation
outcomes.quote: We also provide a list of 18 loci (15 new) requiring further external validation.

outcomes.name: Robustness of tier 1 loci in the no-proxy and no-biobank sensitivity meta-analyses
outcomes.effect_estimate: 75 of 91 (82.4%) genome-wide significant without proxy cases; 56 of 91 (61.5%) without large biobanks
outcomes.quote: Among the 91 tier 1 loci, 75 (82.4%) were GWS in the no-proxy meta-analysis, and 56 (61.5%) in the no-biobank meta-analysis focusing on clinically diagnosed AD cases
outcomes.location: Main, paragraph on diagnosis-quality sensitivity analyses

outcomes.name: Independent secondary association signals identified by stepwise conditional analysis
outcomes.quote: After the stepwise conditional analysis, we identified 25 independent secondary signals across 16 loci

outcomes.name: Genome-wide significance criteria defining tier 1 versus tier 2 loci
outcomes.p_value: P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 unconditional and P ≤ 1 × 10 −7 conditional for tier 1
outcomes.quote: Tier 1 loci are considered genuine GWS signals, with P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 in the unconditional analysis and P ≤ 1 × 10 −7 in conditional analyses within or across loci.

outcomes.name: Previously reported loci not replicated at genome-wide significance in this meta-analysis
outcomes.effect_estimate: 4 loci (HAVCR2, SLC2A4RG/LIME1, FOXF1 and NTN5) were not genome-wide significant
outcomes.quote: four loci identified in the two previous largest ADRD GWAS meta-analyses on European-ancestry samples , ( HAVCR2 , SLC2A4RG / LIME1 , FOXF1 and NTN5) were not GWS in the EADB–IGAP–PGC meta-analysis

outcomes.name: Loci losing significance after conditional analyses (classified tier 2)
outcomes.effect_estimate: 5 loci with P > 1 × 10 −7 after conditional analyses (SEC61G/EGFR, SPPL2A/USP8/USP50, KAT8/BCKDK known; TRIB1 and AXIN1 new)
outcomes.quote: in addition to the 91 tier 1 loci, we detected five loci in which significance decreased after conditional analyses ( P > 1 × 10 −7 ) performed either within or across loci

outcomes.name: Gene-based rare-variant burden in SRC (ADES-ADSP sequencing data)
outcomes.quote: In the SRC gene, loss-of-function variants and missense variants with a REVEL score of >50 were jointly associated with AD risk (odds ratio (OR) = 4.23, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 2.04–8.79, P = 1.06 × 10 −4
outcomes.location: Main, paragraph on index variants and rare variants

outcomes.name: Cell-type enrichment of ADRD/AD association signals
outcomes.effect_estimate: Genes enriched for association signals were overexpressed in microglia across four datasets
outcomes.quote: genes enriched for ADRD or AD association signals in the main, no-proxy and no-biobank meta-analyses were overexpressed in microglia across four datasets spanning different brain regions

outcomes.name: Genetic correlation of the no-proxy ADRD phenotype with other traits (APOE excluded)
outcomes.effect_estimate: Lewy body dementia r = 0.64; amyotrophic lateral sclerosis r = 0.29; Parkinson's disease r = 0.16; educational attainment r = −0.12
outcomes.quote: the no-proxy ADRD phenotype was significantly ( P ≤ 3.13 × 10 −3 ) genetically correlated with Lewy body dementia ( r = 0.64, 95% CI = 0.37–0.92), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis ( r = 0.29, 95% CI = 0.18–0.40)

outcomes.name: Association of the main ADRD polygenic score (excluding APOE) with neuropathology endophenotypes in ADC/NACC
outcomes.effect_estimate: Significantly associated with the three AD-related NPEs and with LATE-NC
outcomes.quote: The main score was significantly associated ( P ≤ 2.27 × 10 −3 ) with the three AD-related NPEs and with LATE-NC in the ADC/NACC dataset

outcomes.name: Association of the ADRD polygenic scores with cerebrovascular neuropathology, hippocampal sclerosis and Lewy bodies
outcomes.quote: None of the scores was significantly associated with cerebrovascular NPEs, hippocampal sclerosis or Lewy bodies

outcomes.name: Risk of Braak stage >4 and moderate-to-severe neuritic amyloid plaque pathology at death by polygenic score decile (ADC/NACC)
outcomes.effect_estimate: Tenth decile: 2.05-fold increased risk for Braak stage >4 and 1.96-fold for moderate-to-severe neuritic plaques versus the median quintile; first decile: 0.47-fold and 0.43-fold
outcomes.quote: individuals in the tenth decile had a risk increased by 2.05-fold (95% CI = 1.47–2.85) and 1.96-fold (95% CI = 1.39–2.78) for Braak stage of >4 and moderate-to-severe neuritic amyloid plaque pathology at death, respectively

outcomes.name: Variance in neuropathology explained by the main polygenic score
outcomes.effect_estimate: Nagelkerke's pseudo-R2 of 3.98% for Braak stage and 4.37% for CERAD score
outcomes.quote: the variance explained by the score remained low—Nagelkerke’s pseudo- R -squared ( R 2 ) was 3.98% and 4.37% for Braak stage and CERAD score, respectively

primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The discovery analysis succeeded on its own terms: the consensus meta-analysis identified 91 tier 1 genome-wide significant loci for ADRD risk, 16 of them new in European-ancestry samples, with 56 detected among clinically diagnosed AD cases.
primary_endpoint_status.quote: In summary, this consensus meta-analysis identified 91 genetic loci associated with ADRD risk, including 16 new loci in European-ancestry samples, and 56 of the loci were associated with the risk of clinically diagnosed AD.

multiplicity.approach: Genome-wide significance threshold of P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 for tier 1 loci, with a further requirement of P ≤ 1 × 10 −7 in conditional analyses; secondary signals defined at P = 1 × 10 −5 by GCTA COJO stepwise conditional analysis; Bonferroni corrections applied for the rare-variant gene-based tests (P < 9.8 × 10 −4 for 51 tests), the polygenic score–neuropathology analyses (P < 2.27 × 10 −3 for 22 tests) and the genetic correlations (P < 3.13 × 10 −3 for 16 phenotypes)
multiplicity.quote: An association was considered significant if the P value was <2.27 × 10 −3 , corresponding to a Bonferroni correction for 22 tests (11 NPEs analyzed in two studies).

limitations: Biobank and proxy phenotyping is less specific: 'This strategy increases the power to identify AD loci but also can blur the distinction between AD and non-AD dementia signals, as the AD phenotype definition is less specific in those samples.'

18 loci (15 new) are classified as tier 2 and require further external validation, either because significance fell after conditional analyses or because they were genome-wide significant only in sensitivity meta-analyses.

'Genetic correlation with ADRD could not be reliably assessed for most of the 11 neuropathology endophenotypes (NPEs) examined, due to limited study sample sizes and/or low heritability of these traits'

For the null PGS–Lewy body result, 'we cannot exclude other explanations, such as a lack of statistical power of the PGS analysis or misdiagnoses among AD and Lewy body dementia cases, impacting genetic correlation.'
'the variance explained by the score remained low'
'Such results are difficult to interpret, considering the limited statistical power of NPE GWASs to detect variants with small effects on ADRD risk.'
The whole analysis is restricted to European-ancestry samples, and ADGRL3 and TRIB1 are noted as having been identified in a recent multi-ancestry GWAS.

'Variants with positions of >80 Mb on chromosome 11 were inadvertently missing from the UKBB-diagnosed summary statistics, resulting in a minor loss of power (~6% effective sample size) in a small genomic region (~2%) for the no-proxy sensitivity analyses'
The ADES-ADSP rare-variant samples and the NPE GWAS samples overlap with the meta-analysis samples: 'These samples largely overlap with the ones included in the meta-analysis.'

'Further studies using larger numbers of well-characterized AD patients and neuropathological data will thus be required to more precisely delineate the impact of each of the loci on AD pathology versus other neuropathologies.'

risk_of_bias.domain: Phenotype definition / diagnostic accuracy (proxy and ICD-code biobank cases)
risk_of_bias.judgement: A substantial fraction of cases are proxy ADRD cases or biobank cases ascertained by ICD codes, which the document says blurs the AD versus non-AD dementia distinction; only 56 of 91 tier 1 loci remained genome-wide significant when biobanks were excluded.
risk_of_bias.quote: This strategy increases the power to identify AD loci but also can blur the distinction between AD and non-AD dementia signals, as the AD phenotype definition is less specific in those samples.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Five loci lost significance after conditional analysis, which the document interprets as a slight inflation of the unconditional analysis, and they were downgraded to tier 2.
risk_of_bias.quote: we detected five loci in which significance decreased after conditional analyses ( P > 1 × 10 −7 ) performed either within or across loci, suggesting a slight inflation of the unconditional analysis

risk_of_bias.domain: Sample overlap between discovery and follow-up analyses
risk_of_bias.judgement: The sequencing samples used for the rare-variant follow-up and the neuropathology GWAS samples largely overlap with the meta-analysis samples, so these are not independent replications.
risk_of_bias.quote: These samples largely overlap with the ones included in the meta-analysis.

risk_of_bias.domain: Bias from proxy cases in genome-wide summary-statistic analyses
risk_of_bias.judgement: The genetic correlation with educational attainment differed when using the main (proxy-including) statistics versus the no-proxy statistics, consistent with reported biases from proxy cases.
risk_of_bias.quote: This is in accordance with previous reports of biases observed with genome-wide summary statistics of studies including proxy cases

risk_of_bias.judgement: All samples are of European ancestry, so the locus set and the polygenic score are not established outside that ancestry group.
risk_of_bias.quote: We analyzed genotyping data from European-ancestry samples across 52 studies

disagreements.question: Are four loci reported by the two previous largest European-ancestry ADRD GWAS meta-analyses genuine?
disagreements.position: This document reports that HAVCR2, SLC2A4RG/LIME1, FOXF1 and NTN5 were not genome-wide significant in the EADB–IGAP–PGC consensus meta-analysis.
disagreements.attributed_to: Bellenguez et al. (consensus EADB–IGAP–PGC meta-analysis), this document
disagreements.quote: four loci identified in the two previous largest ADRD GWAS meta-analyses on European-ancestry samples , ( HAVCR2 , SLC2A4RG / LIME1 , FOXF1 and NTN5) were not GWS in the EADB–IGAP–PGC meta-analysis

disagreements.question: Do ADRD polygenic risk loci act mainly through AD pathology or through non-AD pathology?
disagreements.position: This document concludes that the polygenic scores, excluding APOE, were primarily associated with AD rather than non-AD pathology.
disagreements.quote: the three PGSs, excluding APOE , were primarily associated with AD rather than non-AD pathology

disagreements.question: Should GWAS results based on proxy and biobank cases be taken at face value for AD?
disagreements.position: This document argues that sensitivity analysis in clinically diagnosed cases will become increasingly important as the proportion of proxy and biobank cases grows, and releases no-proxy and no-biobank summary statistics for that purpose.
disagreements.quote: assessing the sensitivity of GWAS or GWAS secondary analyses (especially those based on genome-wide statistics ) in clinically diagnosed cases will become increasingly important as the proportion of proxy and biobank cases included in the GWAS increases

disagreements.question: How much confidence should be placed in the newly reported loci?
disagreements.position: This document explicitly separates 91 tier 1 loci from 18 tier 2 loci (15 new) that it says require further external validation, rather than reporting a single combined discovery count.
disagreements.quote: We also provide a list of 18 loci (15 new) requiring further external validation.
